candidates.exact_span: The City of Farmington shall maintain the formulated two-part best management practice to assist in achieving and maintaining the discharge concentration of total dissolved solids effluent from the POTW to no more than a 449 mg/l net increase over the drinking water concentration.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The enforceable TDS limit is expressed as a net increase relative to an unspecified drinking water concentration; different interpretations of the baseline concentration or of what the two-part BMP requires would change the applicable numeric limit (A) and any monitoring tied to BMP compliance (B).

candidates.exact_span: Failure to identify the specific chemical compound causing toxicity test failure will normally result in a permit limit for whole effluent toxicity limits per federal regulations at 40 CFR 122.44(d)(1)(v).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether identification failure has occurred and how 'normally' is applied determines if whole effluent toxicity limits become enforceable numeric limits (A) and whether associated WET monitoring obligations are triggered (B).

candidates.exact_span: Quarterly testing during the TRE is a minimum monitoring requirement.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of when a facility is 'during the TRE' and what counts as quarterly testing determines whether this minimum monitoring obligation applies in a given period.

candidates.exact_span: A TRE may be stopped if there is no toxicity at the critical dilution for a period of 12 consecutive months (with at least monthly testing) following confirmation of toxicity in the retests.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The start point ('confirmation of toxicity in the retests'), the meaning of 'no toxicity at the critical dilution', and whether monthly testing was satisfied affect which monitoring periods are required (B) and how missing or non-numeric toxicity results are classified when evaluating TRE cessation (C).

candidates.exact_span: effluent toxicity to the level necessary to meet no significant toxicity at the critical dilution
candidates.computation_change_reason: This phrase states the toxicity compliance target for TRE control mechanisms; different readings of 'no significant toxicity' and 'critical dilution' could change which numeric or narrative toxicity standard applies (A) and what evidence suffices to document no-toxicity or conditional non-requirement states (C).

candidates.exact_span: Any results and interpretation of any chemical specific analysis, and for any characterization, identification, and confirmation tests performed during the quarter.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This quarterly reporting obligation applies during TRE activity; whether a quarter falls under TRE and whether absent chemical-specific results represent unrequired monitoring versus missing required evidence depends on how this passage is read.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall submit (to EPA 6WQ-PO) a final report on TRE activities no later than twenty-eight (28) months from confirming toxicity in the retests, which provides information pertaining to the specific control mechanism selected that will, when implemented, result in reduction of effluent toxicity to no significant toxicity at the critical dilution.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The deadline and content of the final TRE report hinge on when 'confirming toxicity in the retests' occurred; different interpretations of that event affect reporting obligations (B) and whether missing final-report evidence reflects a documented no-data state or unresolved required monitoring (C).
